best_for: Java developers and ops teams who need a Java 21 runtime on Windows or Mac without Oracle's commercial license terms, and who may want paid support later from the same vendor.

points.title: A certified OpenJDK 21 build
points.text: Zulu is Azul's build of OpenJDK, tested against the Java compatibility kit. Code that runs on Java 21 from another vendor should run the same here, so you can switch JDKs without changing your apps.

points.title: Free in production, no fees
points.text: Azul says Zulu can be downloaded and used commercially at no cost, under the same GPLv2 with Classpath Exception license as OpenJDK. There are no per-processor or per-user charges and no subscription needed.

points.title: Support and fast patches cost extra
points.text: The free builds come without a support plan. Azul Core, the paid tier, adds support with response times, quarterly security updates within a set deadline and fixes for urgent flaws between releases. Core prices are quoted by Azul sales, not listed.

points.title: Java 21 has years left
points.text: Java 21 came out in September 2023. Azul's roadmap lists paid production support for it until September 2031, with extended support beyond that.

points.title: Two version numbers for one release
points.text: The Windows listing uses Azul's own build numbers, such as 21.54.201, while macOS shows the Java version, such as 21.0.13.1. Both refer to Zulu builds of Java 21.

points.title: Install options here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 18 versions of the 64-bit MSI, which installs for the whole machine. macOS has Intel and Apple Silicon .dmg files, but lists only the current release, so downgrades there need Azul's download site. Linux builds are on Azul's site but not listed here.
